Chilling hours estimated from daily minimum and maximum temperatures

Source: R/chill_hours.R
chill_hours.Rd

Estimates the number of hours per day with temperatures inside the chilling interval [lower, upper] from daily extremes, by assuming an idealised diurnal profile. The default interval (0 to 7.2 degrees Celsius) corresponds to the "0-7.2 degrees C" chilling-hours model derived from the 45 degrees F threshold of Weinberger (1950).

Usage

chill_hours(
  tmin,
  tmax,
  method = c("sine", "triangle", "numerical"),
  lower = 0,
  upper = 7.2,
  n_steps = 1440L
)

Arguments

tmin, tmax

Numeric vectors of daily minimum and maximum temperatures (degrees Celsius).

method

"sine", "triangle" or "numerical".

lower, upper

Bounds of the chilling interval (degrees Celsius).

n_steps

Number of evaluation instants per day for method = "numerical".

Value

Numeric vector of estimated hours per day, between 0 and 24.

Methods

  • "sine" (default): closed-form duration for a sine wave between tmin and tmax. With mean \(M\) and amplitude \(A\), the fraction of the day above \(x\) is \(1/2 - \arcsin((x - M)/A)/\pi\).

  • "triangle": closed-form duration for a symmetric triangular profile (temperatures uniformly distributed between tmin and tmax).

  • "numerical": numerical reference for the sine profile, evaluated on n_steps equally spaced instants per day. It converges to "sine" and is intended for verification only.

The duration depends only on the distribution of temperatures within the day, not on the timing of the extremes. Results are model-based estimates, not observed chilling hours; real diurnal cycles depart from a sine wave (cloudiness, advection, cold-air pooling). Use chill_hours_hourly() when hourly observations are available.

When tmin == tmax the day is either entirely inside (24 h) or outside (0 h) the interval; both bounds are inclusive in that case.

References

Weinberger, J. H. (1950). Chilling requirements of peach varieties. Proceedings of the American Society for Horticultural Science, 56, 122-128.

Luedeling, E. (2012). Climate change impacts on winter chill for temperate fruit and nut production: a review. Scientia Horticulturae, 144, 218-229.

See also

chill_hours_hourly(), chill_units(), chill_portions().

Examples

chill_hours(c(-2, 4, 10), c(10, 12, 20))
#> [1]  9.872169 10.461739  0.000000
chill_hours(c(-2, 4, 10), c(10, 12, 20), method = "triangle")
#> [1] 14.4  9.6  0.0
chill_hours(c(-2, 4, 10), c(10, 12, 20), lower = -Inf, upper = 7.2)
#> [1] 16.29746 10.46174  0.00000
